# Decision log

The register of every product and engineering decision for Accrued, one row per `DEC-nn`. The reasoning, options and owners live in [`docs/plan/09-decisions-adrs.md`](../plan/09-decisions-adrs.md) (section 9.3) and in chapter 01 section 1.9; this file records what was decided, when, and what binds the code.

## How to use this log

- **Find a decision.** Search this file by screen ID (for example `BND-01`), module or epic. The "blocks" column names what cannot be frozen until the row is decided.
- **Open rows.** Decide an open row in the session, taking the plan's proposed option (shown in the row), then change its status to `decided`, set the date, and name the artefact that binds the code. Do not wait for a meeting; `docs/plan/AMENDMENT-solo.md` item 7 applies.
- **New decisions.** Append a new `DEC-nn` row at the end, using the next free number. Never renumber or delete a row.
- **Artefact.** The ADR, SPEC, config file or task that makes the decision binding in code. "ADR for P-nn" means the ADR is not drafted yet; its number comes from [`docs/adr/backlog.md`](../adr/backlog.md).
- **Money.** Rows record the option, never an amount. Amounts are set in the vault.
- **Status.** `decided`, `open`, or `n/a, solo edition` (two-founder governance and the release train, voided by the solo amendment).

Dates are ISO. For open rows the date is the decide-by date from the plan.

## Register facts for DEC-01 to DEC-101 (F-02-T01; SPEC-046 AC-1, AC-2)

The plan's owner, effective decide-by and default-on-silence eligibility for the 101 register rows (DEC-01 to DEC-99 from chapter 09 §9.3, proposed DEC-100 and DEC-101 from chapter 01 §1.9). Where chapter 01 §1.9 lists a row, its owner and date win and chapter 09's date is kept in the note. Owners as written in the plan: **TF** is notanaskhan, **PF** is ayushkbhatia, **N** and **AY** likewise; under the solo amendment (`docs/plan/AMENDMENT-solo.md`) the builder holds every row, and a row marked "never defaults" stays open past its date until the builder records it. | DEC-217 | The word layer's space, cap and empty pages (P-03-T05) | **Space:** word boxes are page points with a top-left origin in the space of the server-rendered page image. pdfplumber and PDFium both apply the page's `/Rotate`, so C4 §3.3's "unrotated page space" means the client applies no rotation and only scales (`image_w / width_pt`); `evidence_pages.rotation` records the `/Rotate` value. **Cap:** the extractor's 200 pages and 5,000 words a page; text is the word's characters with control, format and private-use characters dropped, 200 characters at most. **Empty pages:** a page with no words gets an `evidence_pages` row with `has_text_layer=false` and no object (T13 reads it as `not_scannable`); a locked, damaged or non-PDF upload writes no rows. **Hostile geometry** (security review): a page side that is not finite, not positive or over 14,400 pt is unreadable: its row has no text layer and its geometry is clamped to 1–14,400 pt, so the insert never fails. **Failures never wedge:** a words step that fails after its retries leaves `upload_processing` complete (the backfill tries again), and the backfill counts and passes a source whose step fails (`BackfillInput.failed`). **Storage:** one sealed, content-addressed object per text page; migration 0119 adds `text_layer_size`, which storage needs to open an object. **Backfill:** `trust_layer_backfill:<tenant>` (background) walks PDF versions, then inbox files, by id cursor in batches of 50, only those an extraction could read, so a file that yields nothing is passed once. | 2026-10-24 | `evidence/words.py`; migration 0119; TASK-1004 | P-03-T06, T09, T13 | decided |
| DEC-218 | Citation v2 verification rules (P-03-T06) | **Registry:** `evidence.register_citable(kind, verifier, display)`, once per kind; evidence registers `document_text`, `sheet_cell` and `request_item` (verifier `v1`); any other kind is written unverified `locator_invalid` (verifier version `none`) until its owner registers one. `record_citations(tx, anchor=, claims=, run_id=)` verifies each claim inside the writer's unit of work, numbers the anchor's stack, writes one row and one `citation.created` audit event (ids only) each; the creator kind comes from the transaction's actor (agent rows name the run and inherit `app.on_behalf_of`). **Text rule:** NFKC, case-folded, invisible format and control characters dropped, whitespace collapsed. v2 requires the whole quote, its lines joined by a space, contiguously and on word boundaries (never inside a longer word or number); quotes over 2,000 characters are never searched (`quote_not_found`). The agents' legacy adapters keep SPEC-030's every-line-somewhere rule (`quote_rule=lines`) and the screener its exact rule and stored `quote_mismatch` code; v2 never uses the legacy rule (security review). **Authorisation:** every verifier first authorises the acting principal (`record_citations(tx, actor=…)`, which must be the transaction's actor) for `evidence.read` (or `request_item.read`) on the anchor's engagement; an anchor with no engagement, or a refusal, is `source_not_visible` before any source is read; a source that is missing or in another engagement is `source_not_found`, alike. **`document_text`:** a page the word layer lacks is `page_not_found`; a box with no word centres in it is `bbox_mismatch`; a quote must be a run of consecutive words inside the box (`bbox_mismatch` when it is elsewhere on the page, `quote_not_found` when it is not on it); the region becomes the quote's words, and `quote_sha256` is the SHA-256 of their normalised text. With no box the region is the quote's words; a quote on the page text in no run of words is verified with no region, its hash that of the matched normalised text (AC-3). A claim with no box, quote or value checks nothing and is `locator_invalid`; every verified `document_text` row carries a hash, a region or a printed value. A page without words in the layer (no layer yet, or text only PDFium reads) is verified on the extraction's page text with no region, and a box on such a page is `bbox_mismatch`. A cited value must be one of the region's printed amounts (`1,650.00`, `$1,650.00`, `(1,650.00)`, `1,650.00-`); alone, it lights the word that prints it; `value_text` is the source's printing, never the model's. A version nothing has read yet answers `page_not_found`. **`sheet_cell`:** the extraction's table (one sheet may go unnamed); quote contained after normalisation; value equal to the cell's amount. **`request_item`:** exists (`source_not_found`) and is in the anchor's engagement. **Masked projection:** verification reads the words as stored until P-03-T13 writes `pii_regions`; T13 switches the verifier to the masked words. | 2026-10-24 | `evidence/citations/`; TASK-1005 | P-03-T08, T10, T13 | decided |

| DEC-369 | Masked renditions and masked agent material as built (P-03-T15; SPEC-322 AC-24, AC-25, AC-30, AC-40; P-03 §4.4, §4.5; DEC-52, DEC-322) | **Burn:** in the isolated child, each detected box (page points scaled by the image over the word layer's page size, padded 2 px, rounded outward) is painted opaque in the page's background colour, which is the most common colour of the image's border. The page is RGB with no alpha. The rendition is `upload_previews` renderer `v2` with `mask_version` `m1`. **Workflow:** `upload_processing` v7 `patched("masked_preview")` after `pii_scan`; new runs skip the unmasked v3 preview (`patched("previews") and not patched("masked_preview")`). `trust_layer_backfill` v2 `patched("masks")`: sources with an extraction and no masked rendition get words, scan and rendition. **Fail closed:** a PDF rendition with pages but no scan run is never stored (`unscanned`; the backfill retries). A PDF whose word layer can't be read therefore has no served page. An image, a table or a `none` result is stored with no boxes; its pages read `not_scannable` and the viewer refuses them to an offshore reader (403). **Serving:** the viewer and the three legacy page routes serve only the masked rendition; they answer 409 `preview_outdated` while only a pre-masking preview exists. Legacy preview JSON reads the masked row when there is one. Its `page_lines` are kept only for scanned pages; a line crossing a region is rebuilt from the masked words inside it, and the kernel TIN scrub then runs on every line. Its sheets are masked. Offshore (plain 403) and walls (404) are unchanged. **Agent material:** the reviewer, the matcher and the entry assessor always read the masked projection, whoever the run acts for (the offshore-only switch is gone). A PDF with page text has no material until its scan. Sheets are masked cell by cell by code (`pii.masked_rows`). A cell is anchored by a label in its own text, by the nearest label cell to its left until a non-label value, or by the nearest labelled header above it. A column-anchored bank account must have at least 6 digits, so ledger account codes are kept. The kernel's TIN scrub runs on every page text and cell as a backstop. **Re-announcement:** because material now waits for the scan, `check_upload` emits `upload_checks.recorded` only when material can be built. The first scan of a document with page text re-announces it (`upload_checks.recorded` for a version with checks on a request item; `inbox_file.extracted` for a firm inbox file still waiting; a portal drop's sort keeps announcing its own). It does so only in a live v7 run: an upload with a pre-masking preview is never re-announced, so the backfill never re-runs agents on old uploads. **Verifier:** `document_text` reads a scanned page's masked words and `sheet_cell` masked sheets. A quote copied from masked text verifies; the clear value is `quote_not_found`. A page no scan covers verifies on the clear layer as before: no text leaves through a verdict, and agent material never includes such a page. The display and the moved detector re-read a quote on the masked words first and on the clear words second, which covers quotes verified before masking. **Security review fix round (2026-10-26; H1, H2, M1, L1, L2):** (H1) The word layer is now `w2`. It is in render space: the visible page box (MediaBox ∩ CropBox) with `/Rotate` applied and a top-left origin, which is exactly what PDFium renders. `pdf_layout.RenderSpace` maps pdfplumber's boxes back to user space and on to render space, so the burn only scales. Words are read from an unrotated copy, so text reads in order, and the detector runs in the content's upright frame (`pii.detect_on_page`) with boxes turned back into render space. The detector is now `d2`. Projection, viewer and masker read only `d2` scans and regions, so an earlier layer's boxes are never applied to `w2` words. (H2) Annotations and form fields are flattened into the content (PDFium `FPDFPage_Flatten`, `FLAT_NORMALDISPLAY`) before both word extraction and the masked render, and the render draws page content only (`draw_annots=False`). What is shown is what was scanned. Fail closed: a page has no text layer, and so reads `not_scannable` (refused to offshore readers), in any of these cases: its word boxes and PDFium's own text runs don't each overlap the other within 2 pt; its geometry can't be reconciled (render size against page box, or a MediaBox pdfplumber can't place); any letter or digit is set sideways, upside down or mirrored in the content; images cover 25% of the page or more (`IMAGE_SHARE`), which makes scans with an OCR layer, fax headers or Bates stamps not_scannable until P-11; it draws 40 or more Bézier segments (`CURVE_LIMIT`: outlined text; some chart and rounded-box pages also qualify); (L2) or its words pass `MAX_PAGE_WORDS`. Legacy `page_lines` are dropped on rotated pages, and elsewhere masked by text (every layer word inside a region is replaced by the region's token wherever the line prints it), never by the extraction's geometry. (M1) Sheets stay out of agent material for a client's portal drop and for a run acting for an offshore member (`sheets=False`), as DEC-322 and TASK-1207 had it. An image counts as unscanned content when it covers 0.25% of the page or more (`IMAGE_FLOOR`) and is big enough to hold a legible nine-digit number: 30 pt along and 6 pt across (`IMAGE_LONG`, `IMAGE_SHORT`). This catches a pasted SSN card, a W-2 photo, a cheque and most letterhead logos; marks under that size stay. Such a page keeps its words, so its text is still detected and masked for everyone, and agent material keeps the masked text (no agent consumes page images). Its scan lists it as both scanned and not scannable (`pii_scan_runs`; the word layer object carries `images`), so it reads `not_scannable` (`Projection.complete`) and is never served to a reader who may not read unmasked content. Accepted cost: offshore readers are refused pages carrying a logo above the floor. The 25% `IMAGE_SHARE` rule is gone, since image pages now keep their text masking. (N1 regression check) Two rules were too broad, and are tuned with fixtures, never loosened past a missed TIN: the upright rule now fails a page only for a run of nine digits (single spaces or hyphens allowed) among characters set sideways, upside down or mirrored. Sideways margin notes and a diagonal DRAFT watermark pass; a sideways TIN, spaced or not, fails. The 40-curve rule is now `outlined_text`: a row of nine or more glyph-sized (4–40 pt) curved paths of similar height on one baseline with glyph-sized gaps, or one top-level curved object of 20 or more Bézier segments that is glyph-tall and at least four times as wide. Rounded boxes and small vector logos pass; outlined digit rows fail. Every synthetic PDF generator in `abacus_tools.synthetic.documents` stays scannable with no image flag. (N2) `detect` also reads nine-digit spans of adjacent digit-only tokens on one line (gap at most 2 line heights: comb boxes, `900-70-` + `1234`, `900` `70` `1234`). It joins them as `ddd-dd-dddd`, or as `dd-ddddddd` when the first run has two digits, under the usual label and validity rules, with the region being the union of the boxes. After a TIN or EIN label, a trailing digit run and the next line's leading run that make nine digits are one value with a region on each line. The kernel scrub (`tin_patterns`) also reads nine digits broken three or more times by single spaces, tabs or hyphens (`9 0 0 7 0 1 2 3 4`), as any type by the validity rules. The shaped forms keep their own rules, so a dashed SSN form that fails them is still no EIN. (L4) Legacy `page_lines` match region words without their edge punctuation (NFKC). Like pictures, they mark the page `unread` (the word layer object's `unread`; the scan lists the page as scanned and as not scannable): its upright text is still detected and masked for everyone, and the page is never served to an offshore reader. (R1) An image counts when it could hold a nine-digit number at about 4 pt: 20 pt along and 4 pt across, with no area floor. Only hairlines and specks are left. (R2) Outlined text (`drawn_glyphs`) is any 9 or more top-level vector objects of glyph size (largest side 4 to 40 pt; straight or curved; overlapping or not) anywhere on the page. It also counts a form XObject holding 9 or more paths, or one glyph-tall object at least four times as wide with 20 or more segments. Small vector logos and glyph-sized form furniture therefore mark a page, while boxes bigger than a glyph don't. Accepted cost: more pages are refused to offshore readers. (R3) Any digit not set upright marks the page `unread`, so sideways margin notes with a revision date do too. (R4) The detector's digit pieces take hyphens, dashes (U+2010–2015, minus), dots, slashes, unmappable glyphs (`(cid:N)`) and lone separator tokens between them, as the scrub does. A single hyphenated or bare token keeps its own validity rules. A fragment ending a page carries over: the next page's leading digit run is masked too (`pii.page_dangles`, `continued`). Lows: an EIN split by more than two line heights now has both pieces masked by the fragment rule. Its pixels are then text the word layer read, with every detected value burned out. What can still show is text the detector does not recognise as PII: a TIN with no label and an invalid number (an SSN-shaped fictional value), a TIN broken by unusual characters or words between its digits, a number split in ways the run, wrap and fragment rules don't join, a value far from its label (beyond the line below), or a date of birth or account number outside the label phrases. | DEC-507 | Idempotency keys are claimed, not locked (P-04-T22 security re-review M1; P-36; migration 0214) | The advisory lock that serialised a key held an idle connection for the whole request and could exhaust the pool. Instead `kernel.uow.idempotency` claims the key with a pending row (no status, no response) in one short committed upsert before the effect runs, and fills it after; nothing is held open while the effect runs. Another request finding the row: a different hash is 422 `idempotency_key_reused`; the same hash still pending is 409 `idempotency_in_progress` (new code); a filled row replays. A run that raises releases its claim (expires the row). **Claims are tokens (third round, re-review M1, M2, L1):** each claim writes a fresh `claim_id`, and only that claim fills or releases the row; a fill that touches no row (the claim was taken over) is logged `idempotency.claim_lost` and the caller still gets its own answer. A run releases its claim only if it failed before any unit of work inside it reached its commit (the UoW marks a watching caller before it sends COMMIT); after a commit the claim stays pending and a retry gets 409 rather than a second effect. The release is shielded from cancellation. **Stale claims:** a pending row of the same request older than 3600 s (`PENDING_RECLAIM_S`, far above the slowest keyed effect; a crash mid-run) and any expired row are taken over by the next claim, so a key never blocks forever; a stale pending row of another request is still 422. A BEFORE UPDATE trigger (search path pinned) lets the app only fill a pending row once, release its own pending claim, or take over an expired or stale row: a completed answer is never rewritten. The 3600 s also lives in that trigger; change both together. Lookups stay keyed by tenant (row-level security) and actor. `idempotency_keys` loses its insert-only status in schema-check: the app may UPDATE `request_sha256`, `claim_id`, `status_code`, `response`, `created_at`, `expires_at` (as the trigger allows), never DELETE. | 2026-10-27 | `backend/src/abacus/kernel/uow/idempotency.py`; migration 0214 | none | decided |

Branding, pinning, sign-in, refresh and the connect hand-off's `origin_host` would all have read the ALB's name. **Rule:** one kernel helper, `abacus.kernel.viewer_host`: `X-Forwarded-Host` only when the TCP peer is in `proxy_trusted_hosts` (uvicorn's own trust rule: `*`, addresses, CIDR networks, literals), else `Host`; lower case, no port, no trailing dot; several values, a comma chain or an empty one are no host (never a guess, never a fall back to the ALB's name). **Judged once:** `TrustedHosts` resolves it from the real peer, so it now runs outside uvicorn's `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` (which rewrites the peer), refuses one not in `trusted_hosts` or `*.<portal_base_domain>` (400), and keeps it on the scope; routes read it through `ViewerHost` / `viewer_host(request)`: portal branding and logo (`Vary: Host` kept: the response varies on the viewer's `Host`), the portal sign-in, MFA and refresh routes (the refresh's `Origin` must be `https://<viewer host>`), `portal_context` / `portal_invitee` pinning, invitation preview, link renewal, and both connect starts.
